name: COPA: Football Predictions (AI Sports Prediction Ltd)
one_line: Flippa has vetted the revenue, but about $8.9k/mo of revenue leaves only $629/mo profit (7% margin), most users come from paid social at a stated ROAS of about 2.5x, churn is 40%, the app has not been updated since April and new AI-tipster rivals are flooding in. The economics depend on active ad buying and won't survive a handover to agents at 5 h/week or less.
why: The revenue is verified only through Flippa's vetting, not a Stripe or P&L connection. The listing shows 'Verified Listing' and 'Vetted Listing', and the vetting team 'verified: Revenue, Primary Expenses, Traffic'. The monthly P&L is hidden behind a login. https://flippa.com/12822051

The margin is thin. Stated profit is $629/mo on a 7% margin, about $7.5k a year. At $30k that is a 4.0x profit multiple and 0.3x revenue, so a small rise in acquisition cost wipes out the profit. https://flippa.com/12822051

Acquisition fails C4. The listing says users are 'largely acquired through paid social media campaigns' with a 'ROAS of around 2.5x'. That points to most of the roughly $8.3k/mo of expenses being ad spend, and it gives no figure for organic installs. Running the ads takes daily judgment, which conflicts with the claim of 'about two hours per week'. https://flippa.com/12822051

Durability is poor. Churn is 40%, revenue is seasonal around major football events, and there are 1,600 active subscribers. Subscriptions are priced from $12.99 to $89.99 (season pass). https://flippa.com/12822051 ; https://apps.apple.com/app/id6477779829

The product looks stale. The App Store version history ends at 5.0.2 on 'Apr 9', after 5.0.0 on Mar 14 and 4.0.3 on 12/29/2025. That means about 6 months without an update before the 2026/27 season. The app has 4.5★ from only 79 ratings, against 200k claimed downloads. https://apps.apple.com/app/id6477779829
Recent reviews attack accuracy and value: 'Waste of money if pay premium', 'win rate… lower than 30%', and 'Worst paid app. Eaglepredict is free and better.' https://apps.apple.com/app/id6477779829

The market is crowded with new launches, the K2 pattern. Several AI football-tipster apps went live in 2026 with app IDs around 676xxxxxxx (PitchIQ, Scorly, ScorePredict AI, Foot AI, BetGiant), so copying it takes days and the product has no moat. https://appshunter.io/ios/app/pitchiq-ai-soccer-predictions/id6764102973 ; https://apps.apple.com/app/6761887617 ; https://mwm.ai/apps/scorepredict-ai/6761688897

Platform risk is significant. The app is next to gambling: the description mentions a bet builder and plans for 'sportsbook partnerships'. That exposes it to ad-policy limits on paid social and App Store review risk for its main acquisition channel. Exact policy wording for this app is unverified. https://flippa.com/12822051

The price history is a warning sign. A search-engine summary said another listing had asked USD $250,000 with 1,400 subscribers. The current page shows neither, so this is unverified. If true, it would be an 88% markdown. https://flippa.com/12822051

Transfer details are vague. The sale covers IP, codebase, branding and an onboarding guide on Bubble.io. The listing does not say whether the Apple and Google developer accounts, the Ltd company or the ad accounts transfer. https://flippa.com/12822051
verified_revenue_profit: Flippa 'Vetted Listing' covering revenue, primary expenses and traffic. No Stripe or P&L connection is named. Stated revenue is about $8.9k/mo, profit $629/mo, margin 7%, 1,600 active subscribers and 40% churn. The monthly P&L is behind the login wall and was not seen.
handover_plan: Not viable at 5 h/week or less. A plan would be: (1) transfer the App Store and Play developer accounts or the Ltd company, Bubble.io, RevenueCat or the store subscriptions, and the Meta/TikTok ad accounts; (2) document the prediction-model pipeline and the push-notification schedule; (3) have agents handle release builds, monitoring, push scheduling and review replies; (4) keep a human on paid-social budget and creative decisions every week. Paid social is the hard part: with a 7% margin, a few days of bad ROAS erases a month's profit, so the realistic steady state is 6–10 h/week or turning ads off. Turning ads off would probably cut revenue sharply, since 40% churn goes unreplaced. This estimate is unverified.

test_plan.what: No plan: the verdict is kill. If it were ever reopened, the first step would be a free Flippa login to read the gated P&L and ad-spend lines, then asking for read-only App Store Connect, RevenueCat and Meta Ads exports showing 12 months of spend against subscription revenue.

unverified: Ad spend as a share of expenses (inferred from 'largely paid social' plus 2.5x ROAS; the P&L is gated)
Earlier $250k / 1,400-subscriber listing (search snippet only)
The year of the last App Store update, 'Apr 9' (inferred as 2026 from the version order)
Exact launch dates of competitor apps
Paid-social ad-policy restrictions applying to this app
Whether the developer accounts and Ltd company transfer
Steady-state hours after handover

name: Internet Web Browser for Google TV (Android/Google TV app, Google Play subscription)
one_line: Cheap (1.8x profit) Google TV browser app with Flippa-vetted revenue of about €4.9K/mo, paid via Google Play subscriptions, needing 0–1 h/month. Not 'pursue' yet: only the seller's figures exist (no read-only connected data), churn and trend are not disclosed, the listing's numbers disagree with each other, and big free rivals plus Google platform risk are unassessed.
why: The listing is live (HTTP 200 on 23 Oct 2026, 'Inquire Now'/'Make Offer' shown, no sold or under-offer text). It asks USD $117,782 / EUR €104,836, with monthly profit of €4,823, a 99% margin and a displayed 1.8x profit multiple. That passes C3 by a wide margin (≤5x). https://flippa.com/12008497-internet-web-browser-for-google-tv-4-9k-mrr-2-400-active-subs-2-5m-installs-100-organic-99-margin

Revenue claim: 'About 2,500 active subscriptions generate around €4,900 in monthly revenue (€58,465 over the last 12 months, stable between €4.5K and €5.2K per month)'. Revenue is billed and paid out by Google Play. A 12-month stable range rules out a >30% decline on the seller's own figures (C8 partly met). https://flippa.com/12008497-internet-web-browser-for-google-tv-4-9k-mrr-2-400-active-subs-2-5m-installs-100-organic-99-margin

How it's verified: the badge is 'Verified Listing' plus a 'Vetted Listing' section saying the 'Flippa team or broker' verified Revenue, Primary Expenses and Traffic. There is NO 'Data Verified' read-only connection (Stripe, Play or GA). For listings ≥$50K, Flippa vetting means checking the seller's platform access directly or in a live remote session. That counts as verified, but only at a single point in time. https://support.flippa.com/hc/en-us/articles/4842857720079-Understanding-verified-listings-on-Flippa ; https://flippa.com/product/trust-and-verifications

Owner hours and handover: 'about 0–1 hour per month and no own server'. The sale includes the Play app transfer with existing subscribers, full source code with handover docs, the Firebase project and 2 weeks of support. Running at ≤5 h/week with mostly agent-run work (Play Console monitoring, review replies, SDK and target-API updates by a coding agent) is credible. https://flippa.com/12008497-internet-web-browser-for-google-tv-4-9k-mrr-2-400-active-subs-2-5m-installs-100-organic-99-margin

Transferability (C7): the app has no seller face or brand, and the business name is hidden behind an NDA. A Google Play app transfer keeps users, stats, ratings and listing. Subscriptions should survive if product IDs are left unchanged, but this comes from vendor docs, not Google. https://support.staffbase.com/hc/en-us/articles/360003143212-Google-Play-Store-Transferring-the-App-to-a-New-Account ; https://adapty.io/docs/transfer-apps
Paid demand in the category: Puffin TV Browser sells Google Play subscriptions (about $1/month, 7-day trial on monthly), so TV users do pay for browsers. https://support.puffin.com/topic/235

Competition and platform risk: Android/Google TV has no pre-installed browser (Sony support), which is the gap this app fills. But free TV Bro (open source) and paid Puffin lead the 2026 roundups. If Google ships Chrome on Google TV, or changes Play policy, the business could collapse. Single-platform concentration means C8 platform risk remains. https://www.sony.ca/en/electronics/support/articles/00014209 ; https://ovrclock.com/best-browser-for-android-tv/ ; https://www.guidingtech.com/best-browsers-for-google-tv/

Red flags to resolve: the installs stat says '1M+' while the headline and body say '2.5M+'; subscriptions are '2,400+' in the headline but 'About 2,500' in the body; the Play rating is 3.9 from 1.43K reviews; churn, trial conversion and subscription price are not disclosed; the listing date is not shown; and a 1.8x multiple is unusually low, so ask why. https://flippa.com/12008497-internet-web-browser-for-google-tv-4-9k-mrr-2-400-active-subs-2-5m-installs-100-organic-99-margin
verified_revenue_profit: Flippa 'Vetted Listing': the Flippa team or broker verified Revenue, Primary Expenses and Traffic. It is not a read-only 'Data Verified' connection (no Stripe, Play or GA link). Stated: about €4,900/mo revenue, €4,823/mo profit, €58,465 over the trailing 12 months, €4.5K–5.2K monthly range, 99% margin, $0 ad spend. Whether the figures are gross or net of Google Play's fee is not stated.
handover_plan: Days 0–14 (seller support window): open a Google Play organisation developer account (with D-U-N-S if needed); the seller starts the Play app transfer and Ricardo accepts it; transfer the Firebase project; take a full source-code handover into Ricardo's git repo; have a coding agent build and sign a release from the source to prove reproducibility; confirm subscription product IDs and base plans are unchanged and new purchases and renewals are processing. Days 15–45: agents set up monitoring (daily Play Console earnings, subscription and churn export, crash/ANR alerts from Firebase Crashlytics, review-reply drafting); an agent audits target-API, Play Billing Library and policy-deadline requirements and opens PRs; Ricardo reviews about 2 h/week. Days 46–90: agent-run monthly release cadence (dependency bumps, target SDK), ASO tests via store listing experiments, a written runbook; Ricardo's time drops to under 1 h/week. Steady state: about 0.5–2 h/week of Ricardo's time (approving releases, policy emails, payouts), with at least 80% of the work done by agents.

competitors.price: about $1/month subscription via Google Play, plus weekly/daily prepaid options; 7-day trial

test_plan.what: First due-diligence step plus low-cost verification, spending nothing on outreach. (1) Create a free Flippa buyer account and sign the listing NDA to unlock the gated financials, traffic and seller notes. Only after Ricardo decides to engage, use the Flippa inbox (an inbound, lawful channel on the seller's own listing) to send the 5 checklist questions and ask for a recorded live screenshare of Play Console: Earnings report for the last 24 months (gross, Google fee, net), subscriptions dashboard (active subs, new, cancellations, trial conversion), Android vitals and Policy status / Inbox. (2) Low-cost check: install the app on a Google TV device or emulator and buy one month of premium through Google Play (about £1–£10). This confirms the price, trial and billing are live, shows the app's Play identity and developer, and lets Ricardo read the dated 1–2★ reviews for the last 6 months. (3) Agent check of the Play listing: last update date, target SDK, and review-volume trend.
test_plan.channel: Flippa listing (NDA and inbound inbox on the seller's own listing) plus a Google Play in-app subscription purchase
test_plan.success: Play Console screenshare shows net payout of at least €4,200/mo in each of the last 12 months, and the trailing 12 months are within 10% of €58,465. Active subscriptions are at least 2,200, with monthly churn of 12% or less. There are no policy warnings or strikes in the last 24 months. Target SDK is current. The test subscription bills correctly and the app works on Google TV. The source-code build is confirmed reproducible in escrow terms.
test_plan.kill: Seller refuses a live Play Console screenshare or NDA financials. Any month below €3,400 (more than 30% under €4.9K), or year-on-year decline above 30%. Monthly churn above 20%. Any active or past Play policy strike or ad-block or webview policy issue. Revenue is gross while costs exclude Google's fee in a way that pushes the multiple above 3x. The app is not reproducible from source, or the install and subscription counts can't be reconciled.

name: Kliptok (kliptok.co)
one_line: A one-year-old French site that wraps other companies' AI video models. Its stated MRR (€596/mo) cannot support its stated profit (€3,639/mo), 28% churn conflicts with the 'stable MRR' claim, its headline Sora 2 model API was reportedly shut down on 24 Sep 2026, and well-funded aggregators already sell the same models more cheaply. It has no moat, its durability fails, and the figures that are verified don't add up.
why: The figures contradict each other. The listing page shows MRR of EUR 596/mo against profit of EUR 3,639/mo (84% margin), while the title claims a 71% margin. There are 78 active subscribers and churn is 28%. Recurring revenue this small cannot produce that profit, so most revenue is probably one-off credit packs or the figures are wrong. 'Stable MRR' / '100% Organic MRR' is not supported. https://flippa.com/12255808-kliptok-cutting-edge-ai-video-saas-sora-2-veo-3-kling-2-6-71-profit-margin-premium-tech-100-organic-mrr

Flippa's verification is limited. The badge says Flippa reviewed 'Revenue, Primary Expenses, Traffic' and that Stripe and GA are connected. No P&L verification is mentioned, and the month-by-month trend sits behind a login. Site age is 1 year and the business is located in France. https://flippa.com/12255808-kliptok-cutting-edge-ai-video-saas-sora-2-veo-3-kling-2-6-71-profit-margin-premium-tech-100-organic-mrr

Platform risk (C8) has already happened. Several sources report OpenAI discontinued Sora: the app closed 26 Apr 2026 and the Videos API, including sora-2 and sora-2-pro, closed 24 Sep 2026. The listing still advertises Sora 2 as a headline model. https://help.make.com/openai-sora-and-video-modules-deprecation-by-september-24-2026 ; https://kingy.ai/ai-launch-tracker/openai-sora-videos-api-shutdown-september-24-2026/

The business depends entirely on third-party model APIs (Veo, Kling), whose prices and access the sellers of those models control. The listing names no provider or contract and lists no included assets. https://flippa.com/12255808-kliptok-cutting-edge-ai-video-saas-sora-2-veo-3-kling-2-6-71-profit-margin-premium-tech-100-organic-mrr

The market is crowded with no wedge (K4-style). Higgsfield bundles 15+ models from $9/mo, Invideo offers Sora 2 and Veo 3.1 access at $28/mo, and Kling's own app costs $10/mo. https://pasqualepillitteri.it/en/news/677/higgsfield-ai-video-guide ; https://lumalabs.ai/news/higgsfield-pricing

There is no independent customer evidence: Trustpilot shows 0 reviews. The Trustpilot blurb describes a short-form TikTok/Reels video generator, which is a different pitch from the listing's 'premium filmmakers/agencies'. https://dk.trustpilot.com/review/kliptok.co
The 0.5x profit multiple, 92 watchers and 0 comments suggest the market is discounting the figures. That is a reason to distrust them, not a bargain.
price: USD 22,877 (EUR 20,000), shown as 0.5x profit and 0.4x revenue
verified_revenue_profit: Flippa 'Vetted + Data Verified': Revenue, Primary Expenses and Traffic reviewed; Stripe and GA connected; no P&L verification stated. The page shows profit of EUR 3,639/mo and MRR of EUR 596/mo, which contradict each other. 78 subscribers, 28% churn.
handover_plan: Not credible as listed. The core Sora 2 dependency is reportedly gone. Support is about 'prompt quality' for creatives. With 28% churn, a buyer would need constant paid or organic acquisition to replace about a quarter of customers. Steady state at ≤5 h/week cannot be shown, and the listing gives no asset list, provider contracts or acquisition channels.

name: AI customer service chatbot platform for SMBs (unnamed, broker-sponsored, US/DE)
one_line: Revenue is down about 35% from the 12-month average, which breaks the >30% decline rule (C8). Profit at the current run-rate is probably near zero, the customer profile is undefined 'SMBs', and the category is crowded and cheap.
why: Live listing (re-opened 23 Oct 2026). The title says '$4.7K MRR' and the description says '$56,588 ARR run-rate', but 12-month revenue is '$86,311' (about $7.19k/month on average). That is roughly a 35% drop, above the 30% durability limit (C8). The checklist's $6.9k/month figure is out of date. https://flippa.com/14142133-ai-customer-service-chatbot-platform-for-smbs-model-agnostic-80-languages-4-7k-mrr-90-active-clients-zero-owner-hours-declined-from-no-marketing

Profit: 12-month net income is '$9,054', a 10.5% margin on the higher revenue average, and the listing shows profit of '$985/mo' with a '14%' margin. At $4.7k MRR, with contractors, LLM API costs and Google/Meta ad spend still to pay, the current profit is not shown and could be about zero (my estimate). If so, C2 (profit > 0) and C3 (price ≤5× annual profit) can't be confirmed at the current run-rate. Same URL.

Verification: the page shows a 'Verified Listing' badge and a 'Vetted Listing' section saying revenue, primary expenses and traffic were verified. The description says the 12-month figures were 'verified through Stripe'. No P&L is mentioned. Same URL.

Market and constraints: the listing says 'The business has not defined an ideal customer profile' and the customers are generic SMBs. Turning the decline around means marketing a commodity chatbot to SMBs, which pulls toward local businesses (hard rule 2) and toward outreach. The included 'unused 27,093-profile email list' can't be mailed lawfully without proof of consent under PECR. Same URL.

Competition: Chatbase runs from about $32–40 to $400–500/month, Tidio Lyro from about $39/month, plus Intercom Fin and many others. Those are well-funded, maintained incumbents at the price floor, and nothing points to a wedge (K4-style). https://blog.fastbots.ai/ai-chatbot-pricing-comparison-what-businesses-actually-pay-in-2026/ https://www.dragapp.com/blog/tidio-pricing/

Handover: 'Operations are managed by contractors' whose roles and costs aren't stated, and the product includes human handoff. The owner's zero hours probably reflect contractor labour, not agent automation, so ≤5 h/week after 90 days is not shown (C9 is unproven). Same URL.
price: USD $45,000 (reduced 10% from $50,000). Listing shows a 3.8x profit multiple and a 0.5x revenue multiple. Against 12-month net income of $9,054 it is about 4.97x.
verified_revenue_profit: Stated as Stripe-verified for 12 months: revenue $86,311, net income $9,054. The Flippa 'Verified Listing' badge and Vetted review cover revenue, primary expenses and traffic. Current MRR is $4.7k (ARR run-rate $56,588). Churn is stated as 4.9%. Profit at the current run-rate is not disclosed.
handover_plan: Not credible as listed. Contractors run operations, but their tasks, costs and willingness to stay are not documented. The seller offers 'up to 12 months of transition support'. Replacing the contractors with agents would mean automating tier-2 support and human handoff for 90 SMB clients, plus maintaining LLM integrations (GPT-5, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek) and Notion, Zendesk and Slack connectors. A steady state of ≤5 h/week is not established.

test_plan.what: None. Killed. The one cheap check that could reopen it is to ask the broker, through Flippa's own inquiry form, for monthly Stripe MRR and the full cost P&L for the last 12 months. Reopen only if current monthly profit is at least $800 and the decline is under 30%. Not to be done now.

name: Subscription SaaS for Amazon Self-Published Authors | 450+ Paying Members | 70%+ Adjusted Margin | VA-Run, 5 hrs/week
one_line: The product is a points-for-reviews exchange for Amazon books, which is the review-club pattern Amazon goes after. That puts the whole revenue base at platform-ban risk, so it fails C8 durability. The listing's own numbers also don't agree with each other.
why: I re-opened the listing. The core product is a reciprocal review exchange: 'Members review others' books to earn points, which they can then spend to garner reviews for their own titles.' It has 'facilitated over 18,000 reviews.' The listing says nothing about Amazon policy or compliance. https://flippa.com/14387997-subscription-saas-for-amazon-self-published-authors-450-paying-members-70-adjusted-margin-va-run-5-hrs-week

Amazon platform risk, from a secondary source dated 6 Feb 2026: Amazon's guidelines reportedly 'state that customers cannot review products if the customer is a member of a review club that asks members to register their Amazon public profiles.' It also says 'Amazon is increasingly sophisticated at identifying patterns… could lead to review deletion or account warnings.' https://apexauthors.com/review-swap-platforms/

Live 2026 reports of enforcement: a rival's launch post describes 'authors using review exchange platforms, getting flagged for review manipulation, and losing their Amazon accounts permanently… books delisted.' https://www.producthunt.com/p/self-promotion/i-watched-authors-get-permanently-banned-from-amazon-so-we-built-tikiread

A review-exchange community reported mass review removals on 9 May 2026, mostly of reviews posted before April 2026. That points to Amazon purges hitting this category directly. https://www.skool.com/bookvillage-amazon-reviews-1030/bookvillage-review-stability-update-may-9

Author forums report that review privileges were revoked for swaps, and that 'random, sequenced, or escrowed assignment methods that are not directly swapped are also against policy.' https://www.goodreads.com/topic/show/19227389-warning---amazon-will-revoke-your-review-privileges?tab=book

Verification is partial. Flippa vetted 'Revenue, Primary Expenses, Traffic.' Profit is not in the vetted list. Stripe and Google Analytics are only 'connected integrations,' and Flippa warns 'Financials are seller-provided inputs.' https://flippa.com/14387997-subscription-saas-for-amazon-self-published-authors-450-paying-members-70-adjusted-margin-va-run-5-hrs-week

The figures conflict. MRR is AUD 10,609 and profit is AUD 5,414, a 51% margin, yet the page states a 76% margin and the title says 70%+. Using the page's own exchange rate (USD 118,167 = AUD 168,411, about 0.70), MRR is about USD 7.4k, but the card shows $5K. The page claims 826 active subscribers and also '450+ paying members.' It gives 'Site Age: 2 years' but says 'inception in 2025.' https://flippa.com/14387997-subscription-saas-for-amazon-self-published-authors-450-paying-members-70-adjusted-margin-va-run-5-hrs-week

The market is crowded with cheap, maintained alternatives (Pubby $20/mo, BookBounty $4.99–25/mo, Get Books Reviewed $10–24/mo, Get Authentic Book Reviews $5.90/mo, Gemsy $19.99/mo). The listing names no wedge, and traffic is unbroken-down 'organic.' https://apexauthors.com/review-swap-platforms/

On the positive side: the price is 2.6x stated profit, within C3; owner time is about 5 h/week plus an unquantified VA; churn is 6%; and transferable assets are listed. None of this outweighs the existential platform-policy risk and the unreconciled figures.
price: USD 118,167 (AUD 168,411), classified listing. 2.6x profit, 2.0x revenue (as stated).
verified_revenue_profit: Partial. Flippa vetting says it verified Revenue, Primary Expenses and Traffic, with Stripe and Google Analytics connected. Profit is not listed as verified, and the vetting method isn't disclosed. Stated MRR is AUD 10,609 and profit AUD 5,414/mo. The margin (51% computed vs 76% stated), the USD revenue ($5K card vs about $7.4k converted) and the member counts (826 vs 450+) are all unreconciled. Churn is stated at 6%. No revenue trend is given.
handover_plan: Not pursued. If it were: days 1–30, transfer the domain, code, Stripe and member DB, and document the VA's SOPs. Days 31–60, automate points accounting, email dispatches and review-URL validation with agents. Days 61–90, run agents with seller support and keep a human only for member disputes and Amazon-policy incidents. Steady state might plausibly be 3–5 h/week. But the hours that can't be removed are policy and member-escalation work, and those would spike during any Amazon purge. Feasibility is unverified.
